findings.title: Review schedules can be reassigned to unrelated case steps
findings.problem: relabel_blob assigns a numeric schedule to the latest log row with that number, including a case step. Case steps never owned QBank review schedules, but the migration accepts case keys and removes the original numeric schedule.
findings.failure_scenario: A bank question 101 in Pharmacology was missed and has a future review date. The student subsequently answered bundled sepsis step 101 in Physiological Adaptation. Both rows can be classified unambiguously, but the migration moves the bank question's schedule to case:case-sepsis-1. The original review date becomes inaccessible; loading the app may replace it with a newly derived due-today schedule for bank:101.
findings.fix: Determine ownership from schedulable built-in/bank answers, excluding case steps and schedule:false rows. Preserve the numeric entry when ownership cannot be established safely. Add SQL regression coverage for bank/case ID collisions.

findings.title: One stalled write indefinitely blocks all subsequent progress saves
findings.problem: createSaveQueue chains every write behind the preceding promise without a request deadline or cancellation mechanism. waitForFlush only times out the sign-out wait; it does not release or abort the stalled queue task.
findings.failure_scenario: One progress upsert remains pending, as the new __stallSave fixture explicitly models. The student continues answering questions. Every newer snapshot waits behind that request and no further save is attempted, even if subsequent requests could succeed. Reloading loses the entire unsaved interval, while ordinary accounts receive no save-error banner during study.
findings.fix: Bound and abort stalled persistence requests, retain the newest unsaved snapshot, and retry it after recovery without allowing an older request to land afterward. Surface the unsaved state for all accounts. Test that later answers eventually persist after an initial stalled write.

findings.title: A single non-array legacy log aborts the entire migration
findings.problem: jsonb_array_elements is called on coalesce(blob->'log', '[]'). JSON null is not SQL NULL, and neither JSON null nor an object is an array. These values are tolerated by migrateBlob, but this migration throws on them.
findings.failure_scenario: Any progress row contains {"log":null} or {"log":{}}. Applying migration 020 raises an array-extraction error and rolls back the migration for every account, preventing deployment of the relabeling on which the new identity handling depends.
findings.fix: Check jsonb_typeof(blob->'log') before extracting elements. Leave malformed logs untouched for the app's recovery path rather than converting or discarding them. Exercise the migration against missing, null, object, and valid-array logs.

findings.title: Catalog failures hide saved misses while claiming they remain available
findings.problem: The new catalog-error banner says saved misses stay in Review misses, but review pools contain only loaded catalog questions plus reconstructed built-ins. A canonical bank miss absent from the loaded pages gets neither a question nor an unavailable-review placeholder.
findings.failure_scenario: The saved log contains a miss on bank:2500. The bank request fails before that item's page loads, leaving only built-ins or the first 1,000 bank rows. Review misses omits bank:2500 and can be disabled entirely; missesOpen can become zero and the shift card can say there are no misses to fix, despite the banner promising otherwise.
findings.fix: Represent saved bank misses whose catalog entries are unavailable as explicit retryable entries, and do not count them as corrected or absent. Only replace an existing catalog after a complete successful paginated read. Add a browser test with a saved canonical miss beyond a failed page.

findings.title: Ambiguous case-step history cannot be resolved to its actual source
findings.problem: unresolvedCards builds candidates exclusively from QBank questions. legacyCandidates adds bundled questions, but neither function includes bundled or database case steps, even though migration 020 deliberately leaves bank/case collisions unresolved.
findings.failure_scenario: A historical sepsis-step miss with numeric ID 101 shares its category with bank question 101. The migration correctly leaves it unresolved. The app then asks which question it was but offers only the bank question, not the sepsis step. The student must leave it unresolved indefinitely or incorrectly attach the case answer to the bank question.
findings.fix: Include validated case-step candidates using their legacy aliases and canonical case keys, with an appropriate case-review action. Ensure choosing a case does not transfer a QBank review schedule to it. Test a same-category bank/case collision through the actual resolution UI.

assessment: Request changes. The warfarin correction is sound, and the changed screenshots introduce no apparent clinical error. However, persistence and legacy-review handling still contain concrete data-safety and recovery defects. Tests were reviewed but not executed.
